news.title: Oil Prices Squeezed Between Peace Hopes and Iran Escalation Risk
news.summary: Oil prices have crashed about 20% from the late-October peak of $118 per barrel, weighed down by hopes of sustainable de-escalation in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine war. For months, traders and hedge funds have often bet on a resolution of the conflicts, only to reactivate buying when talks fall apart. As U.S.-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia are underway, there are no signs of a breakthrough in either the conflict in Europe or the U.S.-Iran standoff, despite messaging via Qatar. Oil prices have slipped as crude oil flows from…

analysis.summary: Crude prices have fallen ~20% on de-escalation hopes, but stalled Middle East and Russia-Ukraine talks keep upward escalation risk alive.
analysis.rationale: The text explicitly describes competing downward pressure from peace hopes and crude flows versus upward buying pressure whenever diplomatic talks stall.

news.title: Brent Briefly Hits $96 After Trump Says U.S. Has No Need for Iran Deal
news.summary: President Donald Trump declared Thursday that the United States no longer needs a deal with Iran, just three days after suggesting the eight-month war was nearing its end. Oil prices promptly jumped, adding another round of volatility to a market that has spent November reacting to shifting expectations for peace. "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed," Trump wrote on Truth Social, adding that Washington had control of Iran's money and the Strait of Hormuz. The remarks marked a sharp departure from Monday, when Trump…

analysis.summary: Oil prices jumped after President Trump stated the U.S. no longer needs a deal with Iran and claimed control over the Strait of Hormuz.
analysis.rationale: A sharp rhetorical shift away from peace talks toward confrontation around a critical oil chokepoint supports upward price pressure.

news.title: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
news.summary: US lawmakers now want to question Huang over whether one of his alleged relationships was with a Chinese spy.

analysis.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over an alleged relationship with a Chinese spy.
analysis.rationale: The headline and summary focus on semiconductor corporate leadership and national security scrutiny with no stated implication for crude oil supply or demand.
